title: Dysregulated cholesterol trafficking through ABCA1 drives neurodegeneration in Parkinson’s disease
title_zh: ABCA1介导的胆固醇运输失调驱动帕金森病神经退行性变
abstract: Although brain cholesterol dysregulation is implicated in Parkinson’s disease (PD), targeting cholesterol synthesis has shown limited efficacy. Here we identify ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) as a critical regulator of cholesterol homeostasis in PD. We show that ABCA1 expression is elevated in the substantia nigra of postmortem PD brains and in a PD mouse model, with regional analyses revealing preferential alterations in nigral and striatal circuits. Mechanistically, astrocytic ABCA1 drives excessive cholesterol efflux in mice, promoting neuronal cholesterol overload. In neurons, ABCA1 localizes to lysosomes, where it facilitates cholesterol import, leading to cholesterol accumulation, autophagy impairment and α-synuclein pathology. Genetic silencing of Abca1 in either astrocytes or dopaminergic neurons attenuates neurodegeneration and behavioral deficits in vivo. Furthermore, we identify magnesium citrate as an ABCA1 inhibitor and show that it reduces dopaminergic neuronal loss in a PD mouse model. Our findings identify an ABCA1-dependent cholesterol pathway underlying PD pathogenesis and support ABCA1 inhibition as a potential disease-modifying strategy. This study identifies ABCA1 as a driver of dysregulated cholesterol trafficking in Parkinson’s disease, showing that reducing ABCA1 in astrocytes and neurons decreases cholesterol accumulation, α-synuclein pathology and neurodegeneration in mice.
abstract_zh: 尽管已知大脑胆固醇失调与帕金森病（PD）相关，但靶向胆固醇合成的疗效有限。本研究确定ATP结合盒转运蛋白A1（ABCA1）为PD中胆固醇稳态的关键调节因子。我们发现，在PD患者脑组织和PD小鼠模型中，ABCA1表达在黑质升高，区域分析显示黑质和纹状体电路出现优先性改变。机制上，小胶质细胞ABCA1驱动小鼠过度胆固醇外排，导致神经元胆固醇过载。在神经元中，ABCA1定位于溶酶体，促进胆固醇摄取，导致胆固醇积聚、自噬受损和α-突触核蛋白病理变化。在体内，在星形胶质细胞或多巴胺能神经元中敲低Abca1均可减轻神经退行性变和行为缺陷。此外，我们确定柠檬酸镁为ABCA1抑制剂，并证明其在PD小鼠模型中可减少多巴胺能神经元丢失。我们的研究确定了ABCA1依赖的胆固醇运输途径，作为PD病理基础，并支持ABCA1抑制作为一种潜在的疾病修饰策略。本研究确定了ABCA1作为帕金森病中胆固醇运输失调的驱动因子，显示在小鼠模型中减少星形胶质细胞和神经元中ABCA1的表达可降低胆固醇积聚、α-突触核蛋白病理和神经退行性变。
